title: Deleted documents leave their file blobs in the database

evidence.quote: Permanently remove a document and all its DocGit history ... DELETE FROM commits ... DELETE FROM documents
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS objects ( hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data BLOB NOT NULL )
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO objects (hash, data) VALUES (?, ?)

reasoning: deleteDocument removes rows that reference history but never removes now-unreferenced object blobs. Those blobs contain normalized model JSON and original file bytes, so a supposedly permanent removal still leaves document contents recoverable from the SQLite database and does not reclaim storage. Shared objects must be preserved, but unique unreferenced objects should not remain after a destructive delete.
reproduction: Commit a unique document, call deleteDocument, then inspect the objects table in the same database. The document row and commits are gone, but the model/file object rows remain.
recommendation: Within the delete transaction, collect the deleted commits' model_hash and file_hash values, delete only hashes no longer referenced by any remaining commit or manifest, and cover shared-object preservation. Consider a follow-up VACUUM/checkpoint path for actual disk reclamation.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The delete test only asserts that the document disappears from public APIs; it never inspects object retention or privacy/storage behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that commits a document with unique bytes, deletes it, and asserts unreferenced object rows are removed while objects shared by another document are retained.
minimumFixScope: SnapshotStore.deleteDocument object cleanup and tests around unreferenced versus shared objects.
